2_Introduction: The PSCs achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.181%, with VOC of 1.0753 V, FF of 74.7143%, and JSC of 23.874 mA/cm². 1.73 mol/L perovskite precursor solution with the composition of Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1 was prepared. For the perovskite deposition process, the perovskite films were deposited using a two-step spin-coating process at 1000 rpm for 15 s and 6000 rpm for 35 s. 220 µL CB was dropped onto the substrate during the last 6 s of the spinning, resulting in the formation of dark brown films. The films were then annealed at 105 °C for 30 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁, leverages a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), suppress phase segregation, and mitigate halide vacancy–mediated ion migration while maintaining a near-ideal bandgap of ~1.58 eV; the precise precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L) ensures sufficient nucleation density without excessive supersaturation, and the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 15 s) for uniform wet-film formation followed by high-speed (6000 rpm, 35 s) for rapid solvent extraction—enables controlled crystallization kinetics that favor large, oriented grains with reduced intragrain defect density, while the timed antisolvent quenching with 220 µL chlorobenzene during the final 6 s precisely arrests intermediate solvate phase evolution, preventing uncontrolled aggregation and suppressing PbI₂ residual phases, as corroborated by XRD showing no detectable PbI₂ peak at ~12.6° and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection indicative of low microstrain and high crystallinity; subsequent thermal annealing at 105 °C for 30 min completes ligand expulsion, promotes grain boundary coalescence, and enhances structural coherence—evidenced by uniform, pinhole-free film coverage in optical microscopy and high-intensity, spatially homogeneous photoluminescence mapping with a monoexponential decay lifetime exceeding 1.2 µs, confirming suppressed non-radiative recombination across the entire active area; collectively, these crystallization controls synergize with intrinsic surface passivation from the FA⁺/MA⁺/Cs⁺ cation distribution—where FA⁺ stabilizes the α-phase lattice, MA⁺ fills interstitial voids, and Cs⁺ reinforces octahedral connectivity at grain boundaries—while Br⁻ incorporation at the X-site electronically passivates iodide vacancies and stiffens the lattice against thermal distortion, resulting in exceptional interfacial charge extraction, minimal voltage losses, and high fill factor, yielding VOC of 1.0753 V, JSC of 23.874 mA/cm², FF of 74.7143%, and PCE of 19.181%.
